subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` keep fast ACK semantics with UI-only preservation, or should `started` mean the user turn is already durable or guaranteed to progress/fail visibly?
rationale: The source shows the remaining ACK-before-durability boundary, but choosing delayed ACK, eager recorder persistence, or fast ACK with explicit failure surfacing changes public behavior and session/message-delivery tradeoffs.

options.title: Port Durable Persistence Through Recorder
options.body: Rework or replace #80670 so WebChat user turns persist through the shared recorder/session-accessor boundary before or at the ACK/progress boundary, with busy-session, rollover, hook, media, and failure proof.

options.title: Keep Fast ACK With Visible Failure Contract
options.body: Keep current ACK latency but require explicit progress monitoring and visible/auditable failure when the turn cannot be durably persisted or dispatched.

options.title: Pause The Candidate PR
options.body: Do not merge #80670 until maintainers settle the `chat.send` ACK/durability contract and decide whether the PR's broad design is worth carrying forward.

recommendation.title: Port Durable Persistence Through Recorder
recommendation.body: Rework or replace #80670 so WebChat user turns persist through the shared recorder/session-accessor boundary before or at the ACK/progress boundary, with busy-session, rollover, hook, media, and failure proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The key unresolved choice is the shared user-turn recorder and gateway transcript persistence boundary, where this owner trail is strongest.
